title: Atomic turn rework — personal scratchpad
content:
Goal: explore a lightweight "atomic turn" model for user-agent conversation turns that reduces token churn and simplifies resume/partial-reply UX.

Context + quick rationale:
- Current session model stores whole message chunks; for long-running conversations we see repeated prefix tokens & high KV cache size.
- 'Atomic turn' = treat each user-agent exchange as a canonical minimal unit (metadata + compact delta) so we can reconstruct context with far fewer tokens.
- Want to keep developer API simple (no new primitives for customers) but enable internal representation changes that cut cost and improve resume latency.

Rough product hypothesis:
- If we represent turns as "deltas" + compressed referents (anchors) then average session token storage drops by 30–60% for long chats without changing model prompts developers write.
- Side benefits: faster cold resume, better partial-restore for multi-device handoff, fewer KV-evictions during high concurrency.

Design sketch (internal):
- Ingress: user message arrives -> canonicalize (strip redundant system context, normalize whitespace, detect quoted blocks).
- Turn canonical form: {turn_id, role, short_text, anchors:[anchor_id], metadata:{summary_hint, entities}}. (Implementation: JSON-lite stored in minibuffer.)
- Anchors: short semantic hashes pointing to a larger blob (full message or excerpt) kept in cold-store; multiple turns can reference same anchor.
- Reconstruction at serve-time: runtime assembles initial prompt by expanding anchors until token budget reached, preferring most recent + highest relevance.

API surface implications (keeps outward compatibility):
- No change to create-message/send-message APIs.
- We add optional flags: ?session_mode=atomic (server-side opt-in) and diagnostics field in response with compression_ratio.
- Expose a developer tool: session-compact-preview (returns a compact diff + anchor map for debugging).

User stories (rough):
- As an app developer, I want long user conversations to cost less to store so my monthly bill is lower for chat history heavy apps.
- As a platform engineer, I want to reduce KV cache pressure during spiky load so we don't evict active sessions.
- As an end-user, I want switching devices to resume faster (less load time) when my assistant continues the prior conversation.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Server can ingest and persist turns in atomic form and serve assembled prompt indistinguishable from baseline for 90% of evaluated sessions.
- End-to-end token storage per session reduced by >=25% on median for test workload X.
- No change in client API (backwards compatible) and added opt-in flag for atomic mode.
- Debug tool returns compact preview and anchor mapping.

Metrics to track:
- median_tokens_per_session, 95th_percentile_tokens, avg_resume_latency, KV_cache_hit_rate, cost_per_session (estimated).
- Developer-facing: percent_of_sessions_atomic, compaction_ratio_distribution.

Operational constraints & risks:
- Anchors require cold-store lifecycle + GC; risk of dangling references (need reference counting or TTL).
- Privacy/GDPR: compressed anchors still store user content; must integrate with deletion flow and KMS policies.
- Model fidelity: compaction must not remove critical prompt instruction; need conservative summary heuristics for system-level instructions.
- Runtime complexity: reconstruction logic must be sub-ms deterministic or else latency SLOs could be impacted.

Experiment plan (phases):
1) Simulator: run offline simulation on sampled sessions to evaluate naive compression heuristics. Baselines: no compression, naive substring dedupe, semantic-anchor (embedding cluster).
2) Canary read-only: enable atomic-mode in read-only diagnostic mode for 10% of sessions to compare assembled prompt vs baseline output (fidelity delta).
3) Canary opt-in: 1% write-mode with opt-in customers (internal apps) and tight monitoring for fidelity/regressions.
4) Gradual rollout with adaptive thresholds.

Implementation notes (engineering):
- Storage: append-only minibuffer for turn metadata (fast), anchor blobs in object store with index by semantic-hash; master index in Postgres for reference counts.
- Summarization heuristic: combine simple rules (preserve system instructions, keep quoted 'user says' blocks) + light model-based summary (1–2 token-level summary hints using a distilled summarizer).
- Cache strategy: prefer hot-expansion of anchors used in last 50 turns; evict LRU beyond 10k sessions per shard.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we guarantee deterministic assembly order so audits reproduce prompts? Need canonicalization rules and sorting by turn_id.
- Reconciliation for edits/deletes: if user edits older turn, do we rewrite anchors or create new anchor + tombstone?
- Cost model: estimate monthly savings per 100k active sessions for embed-anchor vs naive. Need data team to run sample.
- UX for developers: should we surface per-session compaction badges in Console? what SLA promises to make?

Immediate next steps (notes to self):
- Ask data team for tokenized session sample and run quick simulation (ticket: PROD-9123).
- Prototype a tiny in-memory anchor assembler for local dev (owner: Renata, ETA: 2w).
- Draft short confluence page summarizing approach + compliance checklist (privacy + deletion).
- Sync with Maya (summary heuristics) and Noah (storage design) next Thu.

Random brainstorm snippets (unfiltered):
- Maybe we can let devs tag messages as 'sticky' to always force anchor retention.
- Could use content-addressed dedupe across customers? (probably not for privacy).
- Expose an "atomic preview" in Console timeline that shows which anchors compressed a turn.
- Edge-case: multimodal turns where anchor is an image — treat as anchor with mime metadata and small caption.

End of notes.

-- Renata
quick, noisy scratchpad. will shape into proper mini-PRD after sims.
